# `liber:bluetooth@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:bluetooth` package (`bluetooth.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem Bluetooth - what a client may ask of the host stack, in three separate authorities.  THREE INTERFACES AND NOT THREE METHODS ON ONE, because the difference between them is who may hold them rather than what they do. A component that may LIST the radios on a machine must not be able to power one; a component that may pair must not be able to read a link key; and the input service, which is the one consumer of what pairing produces, must be able to do neither.  NOTHING HERE CARRIES A KEY OR A RAW HCI PACKET. The keys live in a backend this service reaches over a private capability and the packets live under the transport; a client of any interface below sees typed state and typed outcomes, and a component that could see either could be the stack itself.

### enum `peer-kind`

Which kind a peer address is.  A RESOLVABLE PRIVATE ADDRESS - one a device rotates for privacy - is resolved with the identity key the peer gave at bonding, and a bonded peer is always named by its IDENTITY address; `resolvable` names one seen before it resolved, or one no bond resolves.

| case | ordinal | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public` | 1 | An LE address from the device's own assigned block. |
| `random-static` | 2 | An LE random address the device does not rotate. |
| `bredr` | 3 | A BR/EDR device address. |
| `resolvable` | 4 | An LE resolvable private address no bond resolves. |

### enum `pairing-state`

How far a pairing attempt has got.

| case | ordinal | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `idle` | 1 | Nothing is in flight. |
| `connecting` | 2 | Connecting to the peer. |
| `pairing` | 3 | Exchanging keys. |
| `bonded` | 4 | Bonded and durably stored. A pairing is not reported as bonded before the record is committed: a bond that exists only in memory is one a reboot silently removes, and a person told they had paired would find the device asking again. |

### enum `security-level`

WHAT THE ENCRYPTION ON A LINK IS WORTH, reported rather than implied.  This slice implements the Just Works association model, which buys encryption against a listener and NOT authentication against a radio that answered first. A stack that reported one number for both would be telling an operator that a device is the device they pressed a button on, which nothing here establishes.

| case | ordinal | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | 1 | No encryption. |
| `encrypted-unauthenticated` | 2 | Encrypted, and the peer is NOT authenticated. This is what Just Works produces. |
| `encrypted-authenticated` | 3 | Encrypted and authenticated. No association model in this slice reaches it, and it is named so that a client reads the level rather than assuming the one it was given. |

## Interfaces

### interface `bluetooth`

THE READ AUTHORITY: what is here, and nothing that changes it.  A component holding this may enumerate controllers and look for devices. It may not power a radio, pair, forget a bond or make a peer an input source - those are the operator's, and they are on a different interface for that reason rather than being checked by a flag.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `controllers` | `controllers() -> result<list<controller-info>, error>` | The controllers this machine has. |
| 2 | `scan` | `scan(controller: u32, deadline-ms: u32) -> result<scan-handle, error>` | Start a scan. `deadline-ms` is the caller's own limit and is CAPPED rather than believed: a scan is a radio running and a client asking for an hour of it is a client deciding how the machine behaves. At most 64 deduplicated results are reported and the scan ends by itself at the deadline, whichever comes first. |
| 3 | `results` | `results(scan: scan-handle) -> result<list<scan-result>, error>` | The results so far, and whether the scan has finished. A scan that ended - at its deadline, at the result cap, or because it was cancelled - says so here, so a client learns of the end rather than waiting for one more result that will never come. |
| 4 | `scanning` | `scanning(scan: scan-handle) -> result<bool, error>` | Whether that scan is still running. |
| 5 | `cancel` | `cancel(scan: scan-handle) -> result<unit, error>` | Stop a scan now. EXPLICIT, because a scan that only ever ended at its deadline would keep a radio busy for the rest of a caller's ten seconds after it had found what it wanted. |

### interface `bluetooth-operator`

THE OPERATOR AUTHORITY: the verbs that change what the machine is doing.  Granted to one explicitly trusted component through the manifest's own grant path, and to nothing else. THIS IS AN ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATION AND NOT A CLAIM ABOUT THE PHYSICAL DEVICE: that a person is allowed to pair says nothing about whether the radio that answered is the mouse on the desk, and the security level every answer here carries is what says so.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `power` | `power(controller: u32, on: bool) -> result<unit, error>` | Turn a controller's radio on or off. The platform's own allow or deny setting is enforced here and a refusal says so; this service invents no radio policy of its own. |
| 2 | `pair` | `pair(controller: u32, peer: peer-address) -> result<unit, error>` | Begin pairing with a peer. ONE ATTEMPT PER CONTROLLER IS LIVE, and a second while one is in flight is refused rather than queued - a queued pairing is one an operator has stopped watching. The attempt is capped at sixty seconds whatever the peer does. |
| 3 | `progress` | `progress(controller: u32) -> result<pairing-progress, error>` | How the live attempt is going. |
| 4 | `cancel` | `cancel(controller: u32) -> result<unit, error>` | Abandon the live attempt. |
| 5 | `bonded` | `bonded(controller: u32) -> result<list<bonded-peer>, error>` | The peers this machine is bonded to. |
| 6 | `forget` | `forget(controller: u32, peer: peer-address) -> result<unit, error>` | Delete a bond. DURABLY, AND BEFORE THIS ANSWERS: a forget that reported success and left the record on the volume is a device an operator believes is gone and which reconnects after a reboot. The live link is terminated with it. |
| 7 | `enable` | `enable(controller: u32, peer: peer-address, on: bool) -> result<unit, error>` | Make a bonded peer an input source, or stop it being one. Disabling closes whatever channel the input service holds for it. The same as trusting it for input. |
| 8 | `prompts` | `prompts(controller: u32) -> result<stream<pairing-prompt>, error>` | THE PROMPT WATCHER: a stream of this controller's pairing prompts. While one is open the controller is pairable and declares the IO capabilities a person can answer; one watcher per controller, a second refused. |
| 9 | `answer` | `answer(controller: u32, prompt: u32, reply: prompt-reply) -> result<unit, error>` | Answer a prompt. A reply that does not fit the question, or comes after the deadline, is refused. |
| 10 | `discoverable` | `discoverable(controller: u32, seconds: u32) -> result<unit, error>` | Make the classic radio discoverable for at most 180 seconds; zero ends it. |
| 11 | `trust` | `trust(controller: u32, peer: peer-address, profile: profile, on: bool) -> result<unit, error>` | Trust a bonded peer for a profile, or stop trusting it. |
| 12 | `alias` | `alias(controller: u32, peer: peer-address, alias: string) -> result<unit, error>` | The operator's name for a bonded peer: what an application grant names it by. Empty clears it. |
| 13 | `devices` | `devices(controller: u32) -> result<list<device-status>, error>` | Every device this controller knows - bonded, connected or found - on both radios. |
| 14 | `connect` | `connect(controller: u32, peer: peer-address, profile: profile) -> result<unit, error>` | Connect a bonded peer's profile, or disconnect it. |
| 15 | `disconnect` | `disconnect(controller: u32, peer: peer-address, profile: profile) -> result<unit, error>` |  |
| 16 | `pair-legacy` | `pair-legacy(controller: u32, peer: peer-address) -> result<unit, error>` | Pair with legacy PIN entry: only for a device that cannot do better, and never over a better bond. |
| 17 | `media` | `media(controller: u32, peer: peer-address, command: media-command) -> result<unit, error>` | THE REMOTE CONTROL, toward a phone playing to this system: a button pressed and let go over AVRCP. |
| 18 | `send` | `send(controller: u32, peer: peer-address, name: string, length: option<u64>) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` | PUSH ONE OBJECT to a bonded peer over OBEX Object Push - on L2CAP where the peer's record offers it, on RFCOMM otherwise - named `name`, of `length` bytes where the caller knows it. The object's bytes go on the returned `object-push`: THIS SERVICE HOLDS NO STORAGE AUTHORITY, and reads no file - `btctl send` forwards the stream the shell's input redirection opened. |
| 19 | `receive` | `receive(controller: u32, peer: peer-address, max-bytes: u64) -> result<stream<received-object>, error>` | RECEIVE THE ONE OBJECT the bonded `peer` pushes while this waits - at most `max-bytes` of it, for at most 180 seconds or until the stream is closed. While it waits the peer's page and its Object Push channel are admitted, and nobody else's; an object that declares more than `max-bytes` is refused before a byte of it is taken, and one that passes it while arriving is aborted. CONSENTED BY THE CALL: no prompt is raised. One receiver per controller. |
| 20 | `connect-pan` | `connect-pan(controller: u32, peer: peer-address, replace-uplink: bool) -> result<unit, error>` | TETHER TO A BONDED PEER'S NETWORK ACCESS POINT as a PAN user, the link offered to NetworkService - which may make it the uplink in place of a selected one only where `replace-uplink` says so; otherwise it is held, unselected, while another is selected. `connect` with `pan` is this without `replace-uplink`. |
| 21 | `broadcast-scan` | `broadcast-scan(controller: u32, seconds: u32) -> result<unit, error>` | LOOK FOR LE AUDIO BROADCASTS for at most `seconds` (30 at most): their announcements gathered for `broadcasts`. |
| 22 | `broadcasts` | `broadcasts(controller: u32) -> result<list<broadcast-source>, error>` | The broadcasts heard by the last `broadcast-scan`, so far. |
| 23 | `broadcast-play` | `broadcast-play(controller: u32, broadcast-id: u32, code: list<u8>) -> result<unit, error>` | PLAY ONE: its periodic train joined, its BASE read, its BIG synchronised - with `code` where it is encrypted, empty where it is not - and its streams offered to AudioService as a route to the default output, as a phone's A2DP stream is. One broadcast at a time; a second replaces the first. |
| 24 | `broadcast-stop` | `broadcast-stop(controller: u32) -> result<unit, error>` | Stop the broadcast being played. |

### interface `object-push`

AN OBJECT BEING PUSHED, from `bluetooth-operator.send`: its bytes, then its end.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `write` | `write(data: list<u8>) -> result<u64, error>` | The object's next bytes, and how many were taken: `again` while the push holds as much as it may and the peer has not taken it, `closed` once the push is over. |
| 2 | `finish` | `finish() -> result<u64, error>` | The object's end. Answered when the peer has it - with the bytes it took - or with why it does not: `denied` for a peer that refused it, `not-found` for one that offers no Object Push, `timed-out` for one that never answered, `closed` for a link lost. |
| 3 | `abort` | `abort() -> result<unit, error>` | Abandon it. |

### interface `bluetooth-profile`

THE PROFILE AUTHORITY: one verb, over peers an operator has already trusted for input.  Held by the input service and by nothing else. It cannot scan, cannot pair, cannot enumerate bonds and cannot reach a peer the operator has not trusted - so the component that consumes input has no authority over the radio that produces it.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `open-input` | `open-input(controller: u32, peer: peer-address) -> result<stream<input-report>, error>` | A bounded stream of decoded reports from one peer trusted for input, on either radio: pointer motion, key transitions with their page, and gamepad frames. Refused for a peer that is not bonded or not trusted for input. The stream ends when the trust is withdrawn, when the link is lost, or when the controller's session ends - and a consumer learns of all three the same way. |
| 2 | `enabled` | `enabled() -> result<list<enabled-peer>, error>` | The peers `open-input` would accept right now: bonded and trusted for input, on every controller. WITHOUT IT THE ONE CONSUMER OF THIS INTERFACE COULD NOT FIND WHAT IT IS ALLOWED TO OPEN, and handing it the operator's bonded list would hand it the verbs that come with it. |

### interface `bluetooth-gatt`

AN APPLICATION'S GATT CLIENT, minted per launch by PermissionManager for one component, one bonded peer the operator gave an alias and trusted for GATT, and a set of services. IT REACHES NOTHING OUTSIDE THOSE SERVICES - and never a service the stack drives itself: HID, GAP, GATT and the LE Audio services - and it ends with the launch. While the peer is not connected every operation answers `closed`.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `services` | `services() -> result<list<gatt-service>, error>` | The granted services the peer has. |
| 2 | `characteristics` | `characteristics(start: u16) -> result<list<gatt-characteristic>, error>` | The characteristics of the granted service beginning at `start`. |
| 3 | `read` | `read(handle: u16) -> result<list<u8>, error>` |  |
| 4 | `write` | `write(handle: u16, value: list<u8>) -> result<unit, error>` | A write with a response. |
| 5 | `subscribe` | `subscribe(handle: u16) -> result<stream<gatt-value>, error>` | The characteristic's notifications, turned on for as long as the stream is held. |

### interface `bluetooth-serial`

AN APPLICATION'S SERIAL PORT, minted per launch by PermissionManager for one component and one bonded BR/EDR peer the operator gave an alias and trusted for the serial port profile: a byte stream over RFCOMM and nothing above it. NOT A CONSOLE - `console-bytes` is a device's kind, and its one consumer is the development agent. It ends with the launch, and the channel it opened closes with it.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `connect` | `connect() -> result<unit, error>` | Connect the port: the peer paged where it has no link, its record searched for the serial port and the RFCOMM channel the record names opened. Answered when the channel is open - at once where it is - or with why it is not: `not-found` for a peer that offers no serial port, `timed-out` for one that never answered. |
| 2 | `write` | `write(data: list<u8>) -> result<u32, error>` | Bytes to the peer, and how many were taken: as many as the channel's queue holds past the peer's credits. `again` when it holds nothing more - the peer's credits are the backpressure - and `closed` while the channel is not open. |
| 3 | `read` | `read() -> result<stream<serial-bytes>, error>` | What the peer sends, as it arrives - one subscription. A reader that falls behind holds the peer, its credits not given back, rather than losing bytes. The stream ends when the channel closes. |
| 4 | `close` | `close() -> result<unit, error>` | Close the channel. The grant stays for its launch and may connect again. |

### interface `bluetooth-admin`

THE MINTING ROOT PermissionManager holds, and nothing else: application grants, each for one component's launch.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `mint-gatt` | `mint-gatt(alias: string, services: list<service-class>, owner: handle<task>) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` | A GATT client for `owner`'s launch, on the bonded peer the operator named `alias` - refused unless that peer is trusted for GATT - and for these services alone. |
| 2 | `mint-serial` | `mint-serial(alias: string, owner: handle<task>) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` | A serial port for `owner`'s launch, on the bonded BR/EDR peer the operator named `alias` - refused unless that peer is trusted for the serial port profile. Minting connects nothing. |

### interface `bluetooth-bond-store`

THE BOND STORE'S PRIVATE INTERFACE. One holder, and it is not a client of anything above.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `lookup` | `lookup(local: peer-address, peer: peer-address) -> result<bond-record, error>` | The record for this controller and peer, key included. ANSWERED ONLY TO THE ONE HOLDER of this capability - "asked rather than read" means a typed confined operation and not a claim that the key is unnecessary. |
| 2 | `store` | `store(record: bond-record) -> result<unit, error>` | Store or replace a record. ATOMIC: a partially written bond is a key that decrypts nothing and a peer that cannot be paired again without being forgotten first. |
| 3 | `delete` | `delete(local: peer-address, peer: peer-address) -> result<unit, error>` | Delete one. Answers `not-found` for a record that was not there, which is a different answer from a delete that failed. |
| 4 | `list` | `list(local: peer-address) -> result<list<bond-record>, error>` | Every record for this controller, WITHOUT KEY MATERIAL - the key field is empty. This is what the operator's `bonded` list is built from, and building it from `lookup` would mean reading every key to show a list of names. |

### interface `bluetooth-fixture`

THE IN-GUEST BLUETOOTH FIXTURE'S CONTROL ENDPOINT. DEVELOPMENT ONLY: it exists on a development fixture bound to a QEMU test device, reached through PermissionManager in a development build for a probe whose policy row grants `fixture-control`. Its peers are numbered from 1 in the order the fixture documents; what it reports is what the far side of the radio saw this host do.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `act` | `act(peer: u8, action: fixture-action, argument: u32) -> result<u32, error>` | One peer acts. The answer is the action's own result: an L2CAP connection result, a record count, a link handle - zero where there is nothing to say. |
| 2 | `events` | `events() -> result<list<string>, error>` | What the far side saw since the last call, one line each, oldest first. |
| 3 | `type-text` | `type-text(peer: u8, text: string, delay-ms: u32) -> result<unit, error>` | The keyboard types `text` - letters, digits, space, `-`, `.` and a newline as Enter - `delay-ms` from now, so a probe can end and leave the shell's prompt to read it. |

### interface `bluetooth-audio`

BLUETOOTH'S AUDIO, FOR AUDIOSERVICE ALONE: resolved by name through the broker, never a role, so stopping the radio stack stops no audio and no audio waits for the radio. Endpoints are offered as they come and go; each is opened as a PCM channel speaking the device-side contract a sound card speaks; levels travel both ways; and the call relay carries a voice session's call state out and a headset's commands in.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `endpoints` | `endpoints() -> result<stream<audio-event>, error>` | The endpoints offered now, then every change, as a stream. One subscriber: a second is refused. |
| 2 | `open` | `open(id: u32) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` | The PCM channel of an endpoint. Opening a voice endpoint brings its audio link up, and closing it takes it down. |
| 3 | `set-volume` | `set-volume(id: u32, volume: u8) -> result<unit, error>` |  |
| 4 | `set-call` | `set-call(state: bt-call-state) -> result<unit, error>` | The call state the voice device reports; none when no session declares one. |
| 5 | `microphone-volume` | `microphone-volume(id: u32) -> result<u8, error>` | The headset's current independent microphone level; unsupported where the profile offers no microphone control. |
| 6 | `set-microphone-volume` | `set-microphone-volume(id: u32, volume: u8) -> result<u8, error>` | Independent HFP/HSP microphone gain, 0 to 100; does not alter the speaker level. Invalid above 100. Returns the actual level after the profile's gain quantization. |

### interface `bluetooth-network`

BLUETOOTH'S NETWORK LINKS, FOR NETWORKSERVICE ALONE: resolved by name through the broker, never a role, so no network waits for the radio. A link opened is a frame channel speaking a NIC provider's frame-plus-link wire - the greeting, `MAC` with the local controller's address and the 1500-byte MTU, then one Ethernet frame per message both ways - and BNEP's framing is this service's. Closing it ends nothing but the channel; the link ends with the operator's disconnect, or its peer.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `links` | `links() -> result<stream<network-event>, error>` | The links offered now, then every change, as a stream. One subscriber: a second is refused. |
| 2 | `open` | `open(id: u32) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` | A link's frame channel. One holder. |
